reader.decision: Approve deleting the `digest_builder` crontab line (line 3) on `ops-box-2` and ticking line 8 in the cutover doc. Do not add the unique index now.
reader.decision_reason: The message traces the duplicates to two schedulers running the same job, and removing the second scheduler fixes the cause at the cost of one edit. The index plus ON CONFLICT is a sound second layer but needs a migration, a duplicate cleanup and a code change.

reconstruction.problem: The `digest-builder` job runs from both the Kubernetes CronJob and the old crontab on `ops-box-2`. The cutover checklist never ticked the item to remove the crontab line. Each run inserts one pending `outbox` row per active subscriber. `outbox` has no unique constraint, so there are 36824 pending rows instead of 18412. `digest-mailer` sends every pending row, so each subscriber gets the digest twice.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Every subscriber gets the Monday digest twice. The message says this has happened since late September. Its worked timeline is 26 October. `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` cannot see the cron run on `ops-box-2`.
reconstruction.fix: Delete line 3 (the `jobs.digest_builder` entry) from `ops/hosts/ops-box-2/crontab`. Tick line 8 in `docs/migrations/2026-09-k8s-cutover.md`. Leave the `rotate-logs` line alone. Optionally add a unique index on `outbox(subscriber_id, digest_date)` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` in `digest_builder.py:8` later, as a second layer.
reconstruction.cost: One edit on `ops-box-2` plus a checklist tick. The index alternative costs a migration, deleting the existing duplicate rows, and a code change.

follow_up_questions: Is the crontab file in the repo what actually runs on ops-box-2, or is the live crontab edited separately and does it need a manual change there?
Are any pending duplicate rows already in `outbox` that the mailer would still send before next Monday?
reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve deleting the `digest_builder` crontab line on `ops-box-2` as the fix. I do not want the unique index instead. I may add it later as a second layer.
